title: How an American AI Company Uses Chinese Open-Weight Models
title_cn: How an American AI Company Uses Chinese Open-Weight Models
summary: This week, we got news that the Trump administration is reportedly considering a requirement for US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models. Any effort to discourage US businesses from using Chinese open-source could be a big deal for both the AI industry and the market, where investors are still debating whether customers will ultimately be willing to pay for pricier homegrown frontier models versus cheaper alternatives. Everyone remembers last year's 'DeepSeek moment' for AI, when a Chinese company released a cheaper model that seemed nearly as good as cutting-edge US ones. So why do businesses actually use open-source? In this episode, we talk to Daniel Saedi, co-founder of Minerva, to better understand how an AI native company chooses its models. He breaks down how exactly his company mixes and matches models for specific use cases, the risk of obliterated models, and the issue of data sovereignty. (Source: Bloomberg)
